questions.text: Is the company established (registered or with a place of establishment) in the EU?

questions.help: Headcount and turnover as defined in Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC.

options.label: Energy, transport, water or other critical infrastructure
Digital infrastructure, cloud or ICT services

questions.text: Does the company develop AI systems, or build AI into products or services it offers under its own name?
Are those systems or products placed on the market, put into service or offered in the EU?
Does the company use AI systems in its work, including third-party tools such as chatbots, copilots, scoring or screening tools?
Is the output of the company's AI systems used in the EU?
Does the company import or resell AI systems made by others in the EU?
Does the company process personal data (about customers, staff or anyone else)?

rules.rationale: The company develops AI and places it on the market or puts it into service in the EU, so it is in scope as a provider wherever it is established.
The company is established in the EU and uses AI systems professionally, so it is in scope as a deployer.
The company is established outside the EU but the output of its AI systems is used in the EU, so it is in scope.
The company imports or distributes AI systems in the EU, so it is in scope.

findings.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
findings.summary: Applies. The AI inventory and classification are opened for this client.

rules.rationale: At least one AI Act scope test applies.

findings.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
findings.summary: No AI Act scope test applies on these answers. Re-run the check if the company starts building, using or reselling AI.

rules.rationale: No AI Act scope test applies on these answers. If the company starts building, using or reselling AI, run the check again.

findings.name: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
findings.summary: Applies to the processing of personal data. Not covered by the Hub in this version.

rules.rationale: The company processes personal data, so the GDPR applies to that processing.

findings.name: DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554)
findings.summary: Likely applies if the company is one of the financial entities listed in Art. 2(1). Not covered by the Hub in this version.

rules.rationale: Financial-sector companies are likely within DORA, depending on their entity type.

findings.name: NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555)
findings.summary: Likely applies to medium and large entities in the sectors of Annexes I and II, as transposed nationally. Not covered by the Hub in this version.

rules.rationale: A medium or large company in a sector listed in NIS2 Annex I or II is likely in scope.
